body.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fit}}\), \(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widetilde\theta_N-\theta_N)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,Q)\), \(\sqrt{NT_N}(\widehat\theta_N-\widetilde\theta_N)\Rightarrow\mathcal N(0,W)\), and \(I_{\mathrm{fit}}\) covers \(\theta_N\) with probability \(1-\alpha+o(1)\) uniformly. The fixed-implemented-staffing derivative is \(A=\nabla a_0-DH\nabla a\), so \(Q=A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\) and \(W=V-A^{\mathsf T}\Gamma A\). The residual question gives \(O(N^{-1})\) effect-centering error; therefore \(T_N/N\to0\) is the weakest sufficient upper-growth relation furnished by that bound, because its normalized bias is \(O(\sqrt{T_N/N})\).
body.justification: The theorem turns same-path rate fitting into an explicit fixed-capacity score projection and states exactly when the diffusion center is accurate enough.
body.gap: Generic nuisance-score projection theory does not derive this model's fixed-staffing derivative, critical triangular-array law, or uniform center approximation.
body.consumer: Keheala-like platforms can report implemented-effect intervals from the same marked transitions used to estimate behavioral rates.
